verdicts.quote: “Every request to the Clay Public API must include a Clay API key in the ‘clay-api-key’ header.”
verdicts.reason: The vendor’s Public API authenticates with an API key header, not OAuth2 (OAuth is used for their MCP server, not the Public API). ([developers.clay.com](https://developers.clay.com/public-api/authentication))

verdicts.quote: “The developer platform is available across all Clay plans, including free, trial, and Legacy plans.”
verdicts.reason: Keys can be created self‑serve in-app or via CLI; no partner or sales gate to start. ([university.clay.com](https://university.clay.com/docs/clay-api-cli))

verdicts.quote: “Tables in the Public API is read-only — you can query and read rows, but not create tables, add fields, or write records.”
verdicts.reason: The OpenAPI shows multiple surfaces (routines, search, credits, me, tables) but not full CRUD, so breadth is core objects, not broad. ([university.clay.com](https://university.clay.com/docs/clay-api-cli))

verdicts.quote: “Clay exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server…” and “Registration is open — there is no Clay-side approval step.”
verdicts.reason: This is an official, vendor-published MCP server with OAuth2 DCR and no approval step. ([university.clay.com](https://university.clay.com/docs/connect-to-clay-mcp))

verdicts.quote: “The default limit is 300 requests per minute per workspace…”
verdicts.reason: Buildable today with self‑serve creds and docs; caveats include rate limits and read‑only/Enterprise‑gated table writes. ([developers.clay.com](https://developers.clay.com/public-api/rate-limits))
